merge_obligations: A change to what the plugin ships (`plugins/marvin/`, `packages/marvin-mcp-shared/`, `packages/marvin-widgets/`) bumps the one repository version with `npm run sync-version <x.y.z>`: patch for a prompt-body tweak or a bug fix, minor for a new prompt, tool or agent, major only for a breaking change. A change to repository tooling, tests, docs or the site alone is not bumped. The seven manifests `sync-version` rewrites (`plugins/marvin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the five workspace `package.json` files) are by-products when their version line is all that changes: `scope.exempt` and `pipeline.scope_exempt_pattern` match them, so they are not contract rows, which is the exception to the rule that an obligation touching a file is a row. A manifest the task changes for its own sake (a new script, a dependency) is a row like any other file.
A bumped version gets its entry in `plugins/marvin/CHANGELOG.md`, which is a contract row.

After a change to the server, the shared library, a widget, a skill or a prompt registration, run `npm run build` and `npm run gen:catalog -w @marvin-toolkit/site` and commit what they rewrite: `plugins/marvin/mcp/server/dist/`, `plugins/marvin/widgets/*.html` and `packages/site/src/data/catalog.json`. These are by-products that `scope.exempt` and `pipeline.scope_exempt_pattern` match, so they are not contract rows. CI compares the committed bundles and widget documents with a fresh build (`verify-dist`, `verify-widgets`), and the site tests compare the catalog with its generator.
Keep `CLAUDE.md` and the matching `docs/` page in step with any change to a command, tool, agent, config key or `.marvin/` path; each such file is a contract row.

gates.test: npm run build -w @marvin-toolkit/mcp-shared && npm run build -w @marvin-toolkit/server && npm run test:fast

pipeline.conventions: marvin-toolkit is one Claude Code plugin (`plugins/marvin`) with one MCP server; every command is `/marvin:<group>-<command>`, and `task-*` (the spec pipeline) and `track-*` (the board) stay separate. A skill-backed prompt has three entry points that must agree: `plugins/marvin/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name` equals the directory), a `plugins/marvin/commands/<name>.md` wrapper (every group except `track-*`, which has none) and an entry in `plugins/marvin/mcp/server/src/prompts/index.ts`; a new skill also gets `evals/trigger/datasets/<name>.json`. A new MCP tool is `src/tools/<name>.ts`, built with `defineTool` and a zod input schema and wired in `src/server.ts`. Committed artefacts match their sources: `dist/server.js` and `dist/marvin-pipe.js`, `plugins/marvin/widgets/*.html` and `packages/site/src/data/catalog.json`. The repository has one version, changed only by `npm run sync-version`, with an entry in `plugins/marvin/CHANGELOG.md`. Server code imports no browser SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`, React, Preact) and never writes to stdout, which carries JSON-RPC; it logs with `console.error`. Subprocess output is decoded through `setEncoding` with utf8, never by per-chunk `toString()`. Widgets take colours only from `packages/marvin-widgets/src/theme/` and never use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Files marvin generates live under `.marvin/<group>/` (ADR-0007). A server test that spawns the server goes through `plugins/marvin/mcp/server/test/_driver.mjs`, which strips `MARVIN_*` and `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, and no test depends on the repository's local, untracked `.marvin/` state. One test file runs with `node scripts/test-one.mjs <file>`. A read-only agent pins a `tools:` allowlist. A hook exits 2 only on a confirmed match and 0 on every other path. A change to how a widget renders leaves the committed darwin visual baselines (`packages/marvin-widgets/__image_snapshots__/darwin/`) stale, and CI does not compare them: report it as a minor finding so that the owner regenerates them on darwin. Code, docs, commit messages and PR bodies are in English; commit subjects follow Conventional Commits.
